full_judgment: 5. In 8 D.L.R. 147, Benoyendra Nath Roy Choudury and others Vs. Jaday Chandra Roy Choudury, the judgment debtor appellants filed a Misc. Case under section 47 C. P. C. objecting to the executing of decree supported by respondent on the ground, inter alia, that it was barred under section 69 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and that no notice under Order 21 rule 66 C. P. C. for determination of the valuation of the mortgage property was served. The Misc. Case came up for hearing but as neither party took any step it was dismissed for default. This was restored on an application under section 151 C. P. C. and a date was fixed for peremptory hearing and on that date again the appellants did not take any step, although the decree holder was present. The Misc. case was again dismissed for default and on the same day again an application for setting aside the dismissal for default was filed which was subsequently rejected after hearing both the parties. Thereafter the appellants-judgment-debtor filed another application under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the same ground as stated in the earlier application under section 47 C. P. C. which was rejected by the court against which the appellant preferred an appeal to the High Court. It was observed by the Division Bench of the High Court as follows:
